summary: Atlas Shell is the standalone Vite frontend host for all Atlas applications: it owns global navigation rendering, responsive layout, application switching, and the AppConfig registration contract that all applications integrate through.

classification.why_platform: The shell provides a reusable technical capability — navigation host, layout engine, application registry, top-level routing — shared across all Atlas applications without encoding any domain-specific logic or workflow. Applications plug in via the AppConfig contract; the shell renders exclusively from that contract and carries no application meaning.
non_goals: Application-specific UI logic or page content
Owning settings content (applications own settings content; shell owns only the menu entry point)
Promoting AppConfig to 00_Blueprint (explicitly decided against — see definition section 16)

consumes: AppConfig registration object from each integrated application (see shared_views.consumes: AppConfig)
Blueprint UI governance: 00_Blueprint/UI/02_UI_DesignLanguage (token system, typography, elevation, motion, navigation patterns)
Platform UI primitives from 02_Platform/UI/react/src/ via the @platform-ui alias (components/, api/, hooks/, index.css)
provides: ShellLayout: a React layout component wrapping all application content with navigation chrome
AppRegistry: a runtime registry that applications register AppConfig objects into
Router: a top-level router that maps registered basePaths to application roots and renders AppLauncher at root
Sidebar: desktop left-sidebar navigation rendered from the active AppConfig.desktopNav
BottomNav: mobile bottom navigation bar rendered from the active AppConfig.mobilePrimaryNav (hard max 5 items)
AppLauncher: root-path view listing all registered applications for cross-app switching
MoreMenu: mobile overlay surface rendering the active AppConfig.secondaryMenu
@atlas/shell module alias: the sole import surface for applications consuming shell types and components
invariants: The shell renders navigation exclusively from registered AppConfig objects — no hard-coded application names or routes exist anywhere in shell source
No import from 03_Application/* exists in shell source files — dependency direction rule prohibits this
Bottom navigation never renders more than 5 items (hard constraint per definition section 16 and Blueprint DesignLanguage section 2)
The shell owns top-level routing; applications own all routes beneath their registered basePath
AppConfig is the sole integration contract between applications and the shell
All visual tokens reference Blueprint CSS custom properties exclusively — no hardcoded hex values in shell source
02_Platform/UI/react/src/ primitives are consumed only through the @platform-ui alias, never via relative paths crossing component boundaries
failure_modes: SHELL_NO_APPS_REGISTERED: Registry is empty at render time; launcher renders an explicit empty state

SHELL_INVALID_APP_CONFIG: An AppConfig fails schema validation on registration (missing required field, wrong type, or missing component); registration is skipped with console.error — does not throw; app does not appear in navigation
SHELL_ROUTE_NOT_FOUND: No registered app matches the current path; shell renders a not-found view
SHELL_MOBILE_NAV_OVERFLOW: An AppConfig declares more than 5 mobilePrimaryNav items; shell truncates to 5 and emits console.warn with the app id and overflow count
SHELL_DUPLICATE_APP_ID: Two apps attempt to register the same appId; second registration is skipped with console.error — does not throw; first registration is preserved

consumes: AppConfig: { appId: string, label: string, basePath: string, component: React.ComponentType, mobilePrimaryNav: NavItem[], desktopNav: NavItem[], secondaryMenu?: NavItem[] }
NavItem: { id: string, label: string, path: string, order: number }
Blueprint UI token system as defined in 00_Blueprint/UI/02_UI_DesignLanguage
Platform UI primitives (TableView, ErrorCard, Skeleton, etc.) from 02_Platform/UI/react/src/ via @platform-ui alias
provides: AppConfig (TypeScript interface): { appId, label, basePath, component: React.ComponentType, mobilePrimaryNav, desktopNav, secondaryMenu? } — exported from @atlas/shell; the stable registration contract that all Atlas applications must conform to
NavItem (TypeScript interface): { id, label, path, order: number } — exported from @atlas/shell; order determines render sequence

consumes: react-router BrowserRouter and routing primitives for top-level route management
AppConfig objects pushed by applications at their startup entry points
@platform-ui alias pointing to 02_Platform/UI/react/src/ for shared UI primitives and the Blueprint token CSS
provides: AppRegistry.register(config: AppConfig): void — validates and stores an AppConfig; on schema violation or duplicate appId logs console.error and skips — does not throw
AppRegistry.getAll(): AppConfig[] — returns all registered apps in registration order
AppRegistry.getByPath(path: string): AppConfig | undefined — returns the AppConfig whose basePath is a prefix of the given path
AppRegistry.clear(): void — resets registry to empty; test-only
ShellLayout React component — wraps application page content with viewport-appropriate navigation chrome
useShell(): { activeApp: AppConfig | undefined, allApps: AppConfig[] } — React hook providing shell navigation state to any component in the tree

exposed_surfaces.name: @atlas/shell
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Module alias exposing all public shell types and components; this is the only import path applications should use

exposed_surfaces.name: ShellLayout
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Top-level layout wrapper: renders Sidebar (desktop/tablet) or BottomNav (mobile) from viewport breakpoint, plus an outlet for application page content

exposed_surfaces.name: Sidebar
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Desktop left-sidebar: persistent on desktop, collapsible with hamburger toggle on tablet; renders desktopNav from active AppConfig

exposed_surfaces.name: BottomNav
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Mobile bottom navigation bar: renders mobilePrimaryNav from active AppConfig; enforces 5-item cap; shows More button when secondaryMenu is non-empty

exposed_surfaces.name: AppLauncher
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Root-path view listing all registered applications to allow cross-app switching; rendered by Router at the root path and accessible via the launcher button in Sidebar and BottomNav

exposed_surfaces.name: MoreMenu
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Mobile overlay surface rendering the active AppConfig.secondaryMenu entries; triggered by the More button in BottomNav; uses elevation level 2 per Blueprint rules

exposed_surfaces.name: Router
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Top-level router: renders AppLauncher at root path, maps registered basePaths to application roots, renders ShellNotFound for unmatched paths

exposed_surfaces.name: AppRegistry.register
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Validates an AppConfig and stores it in the module-level registry object; rejects duplicates and schema violations with named failure modes

exposed_surfaces.name: useShell
exposed_surfaces.purpose: React hook returning the active AppConfig for the current URL path and the full registry; backing store mechanism is deferred to implementer

internal_flow.name: app_registration
internal_flow.description: Each application owns a shellConfig.ts file (in its own src/ directory) that calls AppRegistry.register(config) and sets component to React.lazy(() => import('./App')). main.tsx imports these files as side-effects only — no application logic enters the shell. main.tsx is the composition root: it is the only shell file permitted to import from 03_Application, and only via side-effect imports of shellConfig files. The registry validates the AppConfig schema, checks for a duplicate appId, and stores the config. Invalid or duplicate configs are skipped with console.error — registration does not throw.
inputs: Side-effect imports of app shellConfig.ts files in main.tsx
outputs: Stored AppConfig in registry per app, or named failure mode on rejection

internal_flow.name: component_tree_and_routing
internal_flow.description: main.tsx mounts <BrowserRouter><Router /></BrowserRouter>. Router calls AppRegistry.getAll() and renders <Routes> with: (1) Route path='/' → <AppLauncher />; (2) for each registered app, Route path='{app.basePath}/*' → <ShellLayout><Suspense fallback={loading indicator}><app.component /></Suspense></ShellLayout>; (3) Route path='*' → <ShellNotFound />. config.component is rendered inside React.Suspense to support lazy-loaded app components. BrowserRouter is mounted in main.tsx — Router never owns its own BrowserRouter.
outputs: Active route rendered: AppLauncher | ShellLayout(app.component) | ShellNotFound

internal_flow.name: layout_render
internal_flow.description: ShellLayout receives {children} (the rendered app content from Router). It calls AppRegistry.getAll() and useLocation() to derive activeApp — the AppConfig whose basePath is a prefix of location.pathname. It provides ShellContext({ activeApp, allApps }) to the child tree via React context. It then renders Sidebar (viewport ≥1024px: persistent; 768-1023px: collapsible with hamburger toggle) or BottomNav (viewport <768px) alongside {children}. Both navigation surfaces read from ShellContext via useShell().
outputs: Sidebar or BottomNav rendered alongside application content

internal_flow.name: nav_item_activation
internal_flow.description: Navigation items are rendered with active state when the current path matches the item's path. Active state uses primary-container background and on-primary-container text per Blueprint DesignLanguage section 8 (Selected state).
outputs: Navigation items with correct active/inactive visual state per Blueprint tokens

internal_flow.name: more_menu_render
internal_flow.description: On mobile, MoreMenu is triggered when the user taps the More button in BottomNav. It renders the active application's secondaryMenu entries as navigation targets. It closes on item selection or backdrop tap.
outputs: Visible MoreMenu overlay with secondary nav items

internal_flow.name: app_switching
internal_flow.description: AppLauncher renders all registered applications from AppRegistry.getAll() as selectable entries. Selecting an entry navigates to that application's basePath. AppLauncher is accessible at the root path and via the launcher button in Sidebar and BottomNav.

internal_required.role: Governs all visual tokens, typography, elevation, motion, and navigation component patterns used in shell components

Defines frontend implementation standards (stack, primitives, patterns) that shell code must follow
Source of shared UI primitives (components/, api/, hooks/, index.css) consumed via the @platform-ui alias; the shell host supersedes the 02_Platform/UI Vite host but retains the primitives

external_required.name: react-dom
external_required.role: DOM mounting for the standalone shell Vite application

external_required.name: react-router

forbidden: Logic imports from 03_Application/* in any shell file other than main.tsx — main.tsx is the composition root and is explicitly permitted to import app shellConfig side-effect modules; all other shell files must remain free of application imports
Domain logic of any kind inside shell source files
Hard-coded application names, routes, or navigation entries inside shell source
Direct coupling to application-specific data models or API endpoints
Any component library (MUI, Radix, etc.) not sanctioned by 00_Blueprint/UI governance
Relative path imports from 02_Platform/UI internals — use the @platform-ui alias exclusively
Hex color values in component or CSS files — use Blueprint CSS custom properties only

platform_implementer: Configure the standalone Vite application: package.json, vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json, index.html with the @atlas/shell and @platform-ui module aliases
Configure the @platform-ui alias in vite.config.ts pointing to 02_Platform/UI/react/src/
Configure compose.yml for the shell container as the UI host; ensure it replaces the 02_Platform/UI compose host and is connected to atlas-net
Implement AppConfig and NavItem TypeScript interfaces in src/types.ts and export them from src/index.ts via @atlas/shell

Implement AppRegistry as a plain exported const object (not a class) backed by a module-private _apps: AppConfig[] array; methods: register(), getAll(), getByPath(), clear(); emit named failure mode strings on rejection; no constructor, no getInstance(), no class syntax

Each application must provide a shellConfig.ts in its own src/ directory that calls AppRegistry.register({ appId, label, basePath, component: React.lazy(() => import('./App')), ... }) — the app owns its config, the shell does not

main.tsx is the composition root: import each app's shellConfig.ts as a side-effect (import '../../../03_Application/WorkoutTracker/src/shellConfig'), then call ReactDOM.createRoot. This is the only shell file permitted to reference 03_Application paths.
Implement ShellLayout with viewport-breakpoint logic selecting between Sidebar (desktop/tablet) and BottomNav (mobile); provide ShellContext to the child tree
Implement Sidebar rendering AppLauncher button at top, then desktopNav items from active AppConfig; implement tablet collapsible state with hamburger toggle

Implement BottomNav rendering mobilePrimaryNav from active AppConfig; enforce 5-item hard cap with console.warn on overflow including appId and overflow count; include More button when secondaryMenu is non-empty
Implement MoreMenu as a mobile overlay surface at elevation level 2 rendering secondaryMenu items; close on item selection or backdrop tap
Implement AppLauncher rendering all registered apps from AppRegistry.getAll(); handle SHELL_NO_APPS_REGISTERED with an explicit empty state
Implement Router: AppLauncher at root path, basePath-prefix routing to application roots, ShellNotFound for unmatched paths

Implement useShell() using React Context: useShell reads from ShellContext via useContext(ShellContext); ShellLayout provides the context value; useShell throws a descriptive error if called outside ShellLayout — this is the resolved backing store (React Context)
Handle all five named failure modes with observable behavior — no silent no-ops
Audit and remove the existing import from 03_Application/WorkoutTracker recorded in the system map — this is a dependency direction violation

Document how application Vite projects configure the @atlas/shell alias to resolve against the shell source — each application's vite.config.ts must declare this alias pointing to 02_Platform/Atlas_Shell/src/index.ts
ui_implementer: Implement shell.css using exclusively Blueprint CSS custom properties (--md-sys-color-*, --space-*, typography scale from index.css via @platform-ui)
Implement active nav item state: primary-container background, on-primary-container text per Blueprint DesignLanguage section 8 (Selected state)
Implement all interaction states (hover, focus, active, disabled) per Blueprint DesignLanguage section 8
Implement motion and transitions per Blueprint DesignLanguage section 9 (150ms state transitions, 250ms component enter, 200ms overlay appear)
Implement responsive breakpoints: desktop sidebar persistent, tablet sidebar collapsible, mobile bottom nav replaces sidebar
Apply elevation level 2 shadow to MoreMenu per Blueprint DesignLanguage section 5
Apply elevation level 1 shadow to Sidebar panel and BottomNav bar per Blueprint DesignLanguage section 5

Resolve the stale line in 00_Blueprint/UI/03_UI_Implementation section 11 that lists 'Bottom Nav' as out of scope — this contradicts the updated DesignLanguage section 2 and 10; flag this for a human reviewer before shipping

deferred_decisions: CSS strategy: CSS modules, plain CSS — must use Blueprint tokens exclusively; mechanism is deferred (definition section 17)

risks.risk: Stale 03_Application/WorkoutTracker import in current shell codebase
risks.impact: The self-registration pattern resolves the design-level concern: main.tsx is the composition root and permitted for side-effect imports; all other shell files are forbidden from referencing 03_Application. Any existing direct import in non-main.tsx shell files is a codebase defect that must be removed before implementation proceeds.

risks.risk: AppConfig contract stability: owned by the shell, not promoted to Blueprint
risks.impact: Definition section 16 explicitly decides AppConfig is not promoted to 00_Blueprint. Applications import it from the shell. If the shell evolves AppConfig without a versioning discipline, all registered applications will break. The implementer should treat the AppConfig interface as if it were governed — introduce a CHANGELOG or version comment in types.ts.

open_questions.question: The definition references linspad.net as the root URL. Is this already routed through the Cloudflare Tunnel in 01_System/Access to the shell container, or does the shell compose.yml need a new tunnel rule?
